focus.jnote: The tape is bouncing — but it's a thin holiday half-session inside a high-vol bear, not an all-clear. With Thursday closed, this is a two-day move in light volume: futures on the Dow rose 1.3% while S&P 500 futures added 1.6% and Nasdaq-100 futures jumped 2.2% after markets were closed for Thanksgiving. The driver is a snap-back in beaten-down tech: stock futures jumped Friday as investors returned from the Thanksgiving holiday to buy technology and AI stocks. Vol eased but stayed elevated: the VIX was at 25.29 before the open, down 5.63% from Wednesday's 26.80 close. The backdrop is still ugly — the market regime reads high-vol bear, VIX 26.80, term structure in backwardation, skew elevated. Critically, this is a two-day move in thin trade, and a gap at the open does not always survive a full session. A Sniper does not sell premium into a thin holiday half-session that's bouncing off correction lows with a Fed hike days away — cash is a position today.
focus.notdown: There is no clean 'Not-Down' Sniper name today — the scanner boarded ZERO. Yes, AI/chips are bouncing: Nasdaq 100 futures are up and S&P 500 futures ~+1.65% at 7:21am ET as chip and AI stocks recover part of November's losses. But buying bull puts into a one-day relief bounce off correction lows, in thin holiday trade, days before a near-certain Fed hike, is a knife-catch, not a Sniper edge. The disciplined answer on the bull side is to sell nothing new today.
focus.notup: There is no clean 'Not-Up' Sniper name either. The broad tape just reversed higher after a correction-grade selloff, so selling bear calls into a sharp relief rally carries violent squeeze risk — exactly when shorts get run. With the VIX still elevated and liquidity thin, a bear call here is underwriting that the bounce immediately fails, which is not a probability edge. Stand aside.
focus.why: Why RED? Three things stack. One: P(≥1% gap) at 40% is above the 35% trigger and composite at 58 is WARM — the gap line alone locks out GREEN. Two: this is a relief bounce in a thin Black Friday half-session (close 1:00 PM ET) inside a high-vol bear with the term structure in backwardation — the kind of tape where a morning gap can reverse hard; thin holiday volume exaggerates moves in both directions. Three: the Dec 9 Fed hike is ~99% priced — CME FedWatch showed a 99.4% probability of a December hike, which would take the funds rate to 4%–4.25%. On top of all that, the full-universe scanner ran and ZERO names qualified. Stand down on new credit spreads, or push DTE past the Dec 9 FOMC and cut size hard. Cash is a position today.

risks: Thin Black Friday half-session — the market closes at 1:00 PM ET with no major data or earnings. Thin holiday volume exaggerates moves in both directions, and a gap at the open does not always survive a full session. This is the number-one thing to watch today.

Dec 9 Fed hike ~99% priced — CME FedWatch showed a 99.4% probability of a December hike, taking the funds rate to 4%–4.25%. The hike itself is priced; the risk is the 2027 guidance and whether a January follow-up gets pulled forward into a fragile AI tape.

AI / chip concentration — the week's whole story is a chip-led correction and bounce. The Nasdaq 100 briefly hit bear-market territory before stocks rebounded, leaving the Nasdaq and S&P 500 on pace for their worst November since 2008. A failed bounce drags the whole index back down.

Tariff overhang — the USTR proposed Section 301 tariffs on 14 economies, ranging from up to 15% for the EU, Japan, Korea, Taiwan and Switzerland to up to 35% for Vietnam. Any escalation or new headline re-rates the tape, especially in thin trade.

Oil & Sunday's OPEC+ — crude is positioned to close November firmly above $85, with Sunday's November 29 OPEC+ communique acting as the primary weekend gap catalyst. A surprise there feeds inflation fear straight into Monday's open.
